chapter.title: Ballroom Flip
chapter.sub: Two rooms, one airwall, and a system that still thinks there's one room.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the season map ahead of its production-bible entry · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 2 · EPISODE 6 · DRAFT  Comedy cold open · Leah and Maya · Level L3  “Easy one,” Leah said. “Two rooms, one airwall.” Forty-three minutes before the keynote, half the ballroom is silent and nobody touched anything.  ⚑ RV-50 · RV-51: the hotel's room-combine system is a SIGNAL model, and it belongs to the hotel. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Who Touched It?
items.stakes: Four hundred seats and the association's president in Room A. It's silent. A DO NOT REMOVE label is wrapped around a vacuum wheel.
items.reward: Two rooms, each hearing only itself. A label that says what it actually wants.

objectives.text: Pick your first move with three alibis
Work out who really took the cable
Give the keynote the only working bus
Change the state without dropping the program
Look closer: two witnesses nobody questioned

items.rumor: Three people have perfect alibis. One of them is a vacuum cleaner.

items.sub: A hotel ballroom · Thursday · 12:47 p.m. · 43 minutes to the keynote

items.alt: A hotel ballroom split in two by a closed airwall; chips read Room A · Keynote and Room B · Lunch. Maya stares at an empty spot on the floor. Leah is on her headset.

bubbles.text: My label's gone. “DO NOT REMOVE.” And the cable it was on.
Room A is dead silent. The keynote's at one-thirty. Tell me that's related.

items.caption: Room A: 400 seats and the association's president. Room B: 300 sponsors, already eating.

items.alt: Three people in a row: the banquet captain with open hands, a houseperson beside an upright vacuum, and Jordan with his arms up.

bubbles.text: My team set four hundred chairs. Nobody touched your wires.
I was at catering. I touched a sandwich.

items.caption: The houseperson says nothing. The vacuum says nothing either.

lines.text: I was at catering. I touched a sandwich. The sandwich can vouch for me.
It was a very good sandwich.

items.alt: Close on the vacuum's front wheel. A strip of white label tape is wound round it, reading DO NOT RE…. Maya points at it.

bubbles.text: Found the label.

items.caption: One clue down. It's wrapped round a vacuum wheel, which is not where Maya put it.

items.title: The fourth witness
items.body: Wrapped around the rear wheel: Maya's label, and six inches of the hotel's sensor lead — not her cable at all. The houseperson who ran it says nothing. He's been told for eleven years that the wire people get angry.

items.prompt: 12:48. Room A is silent. The label is on a vacuum. The cable is missing. Your first move?
items.happening: The airwall closed at 12:45. Room A — the keynote room — plays none of Maya's feed.
known: ◉ Room A silent for our feed
◉ Label found on a vacuum wheel
unknown: Which cable the label was on
What state the house system is in
items.risk: 400 people and the association's president in Room A; 300 sponsors in Room B.
timeout: Leah re-patches your feed herself, into the first plate she finds. The sponsors get walk-in music over their soup.
When nobody decides, somebody guesses. Reading the panel cost nothing and touched nothing.

hints.text: Before you touch a cable, ask the system what it thinks the room is.
A divisible room has a state. Where would it show?

options.label: Find out who pulled it
options.result: Ten minutes of “not me.” The banquet captain stops answering your radio.
options.consequence: You know less than when you started, and the hotel team trusts you less.
options.fail: Blame spends the clock and the people you'll need in twenty minutes.

options.label: Read the state: Room A's house panel, then listen in both rooms
options.result: Room A's panel reads COMBINED · WALL OPEN. Room B sounds normal. In silent Room A, faintly: the lunch emcee's voice.
options.consequence: The wall is closed. The system doesn't know it.

options.label: Plug your feed into a different wall plate and see
options.result: You try the tie-in plate in Room B. The sponsors' lunch suddenly gets your walk-in music at full level.
options.consequence: Room A is still silent from where the captain is standing.
options.fail: Re-patching by guess fixed nothing and broke the room that worked.

options.label: Turn your console outputs up
options.result: The meters hit the top. Room A stays silent.
options.fail: Nothing you send is reaching those speakers. Louder just makes the eventual fix dangerous.

items.text: Act I — “The room thinks it's one room”

items.alt: Close on Room A's house touch panel, mounted beside the closed airwall: COMBINED, and under it, WALL: OPEN. Maya reads it with her notebook out.
items.caption: The wall is closed. The hotel's system says it's open.

evidence.label: Room A panel · COMBINED · WALL OPEN

items.alt: Room A, empty chairs. From the ceiling loudspeakers above Room A comes a faint voice from the other side of the wall. Maya cups her ear.

bubbles.who: Lunch emcee, through Room A's ceiling
bubbles.text: …and a big thank-you to our dessert sponsors…
Room A isn't silent. It's playing Room B.

items.caption: Silent for our feed. Not silent for theirs.

items.alt: Maya points to wall plate A. Her own feed cable is plugged in, tagged HALYARD → A. Leah, on the radio, looks at it.

bubbles.text: Then it's your feed to Room A. Re-run it.
My feed's right here. Plugged in. A tester at the plate reads signal.

items.caption: So what was the label on?

items.alt: Flashback, 7:10 that morning. At the airwall's stacking pocket, the hotel's house tech holds a short cable running from a small SENSOR box. Maya has her label maker.

bubbles.text: That lead is the wall's brain. Sensor says closed, the system divides. Says open: one big room.
Then it gets a label.

items.caption: 7:10 a.m. Maya labels the hotel's sensor lead: DO NOT REMOVE. She tells no one who has to move it.

items.title: Nobody took our cable. The wall did.
items.body: The label was on the hotel's airwall sensor lead, down in the stacking pocket. To stack the panels, the wall crew had to unplug it — that's their job, and they did it right. With the sensor unplugged, the hotel's processor still believes the wall is open, so it stays COMBINED: every zone plays Room B's plates, and Room A's plates — including Maya's keynote feed — are ignored. The emcee in Room A's ceiling was the clue.
items.label: Test: reason from the new fact before you read on.

items.alt: The sensor lead, coiled neatly on the dessert cart among the tarts. The banquet captain gestures at it; Maya nods.

bubbles.text: It was in the pocket. Panels don't stack on a cable.
You did exactly the right thing. My label didn't.

items.caption: A label that says DO NOT REMOVE on something that must be removed isn't a plan. It's a wish.

items.prompt: (arms folded) It was in the pocket. Panels don't stack on a cable. We did our job.

options.label: “You did exactly the right thing. My label didn't.”
options.reply: (He blinks. Nobody from AV has ever said that to him.) …Good. Thank you.

options.label: “You should have called us.”
options.reply: Called who? Your label said DO NOT REMOVE. It didn't say who.

items.prompt: The hotel's sensor lead is on the dessert cart. The pocket is two steps away. Now what?
items.happening: The sensor lead is found. The system is still COMBINED.
unknown: When the house tech can come

options.label: Plug it back in yourself — it's just a plug
options.result: The system flips to DIVIDED instantly. Room A gets your walk-in music; the hotel tech, arriving later, finds his wall reconfigured by a guest.
options.consequence: It worked this time. You changed someone else's system without asking, and you'll do it mid-keynote next time.
options.fail: It's the hotel's system and a state change. The owner decides when it changes.

options.label: Radio the house tech: what you found, what you didn't touch, what you need
options.result: “Sensor lead's out of the Room A pocket, panel says WALL OPEN, I haven't touched it.” — “Good. Don't. I'm at a wedding across the property. Forty minutes, maybe.”
options.consequence: The owner knows. The clock is now the problem.

options.label: Keep pressing DIVIDE on the panel
options.result: WALL OPEN — CANNOT DIVIDE. Again. And again.
options.consequence: The interlock is doing its job.
options.fail: The panel can't overrule the sensor. That's the design, and it's a good one.

options.label: Ask the wall crew to open the wall and close it again
options.result: Fifteen minutes of panels moving through the lunch service.
options.consequence: The sensor is still unplugged at the end of it.
options.fail: Re-running the change doesn't fix the thing the change unplugged.

items.alt: Split panel: Maya on the radio in the ballroom; inset, the house tech in another venue with a wedding in progress, radio to his ear.

bubbles.text: Sensor lead's out of the Room A pocket. Panel says WALL OPEN. I haven't touched it.
Good. Don't. The couple's mid-vows and my projector just died. Forty minutes, maybe.

items.caption: The keynote walks on in forty-one.

items.label: **First failure point:** the feed leaves the console and reaches the plate. Where does it stop?

items.sub: Beginner · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Jordan and Maya beside a board. Reverberation is the room still ringing after the sound stops. RT-sixty is how long it takes to fall sixty decibels. And you can predict it? Sabine: point-one-six-one times volume over absorption. Five hundred cubic metres, fifty square metres of absorption: about one point six seconds.

bubbles.text: Reverberation is the room still ringing after the sound stops. RT-sixty is how long it takes to fall sixty decibels.
And you can predict it?
Sabine: point-one-six-one times volume over absorption. Five hundred cubic metres, fifty square metres of absorption: about one point six seconds.

items.caption: Beginner: the term, what it means, the formula — and one worked example out loud.

items.text: 📘 RAY'S NOTEBOOK · BEGINNER  Terms    Reverberation   Sound persisting in a room after the source stops, from many reflections.   Room standard   The written specification every meeting room follows.   Formula, variables and a worked example   ƒ FORMULA · Sabine reverberation time  RT 60  = 0.161 × V ÷ A   RT 60   time for sound to fall 60 dB, s  V  room volume, m³  A  total absorption, m² (sabins)    Worked example.  A 500 m³ room with 50 m² of absorption: 0.161 × 500 ÷ 50 ≈ 1.6 s.

items.caption: In COMBINED, whoever is on plate B owns every loudspeaker in the ballroom.

items.title: Symphony Hall
items.body: Boston's Symphony Hall, opened in 1900, was the first hall designed with Sabine's formula. Hotel ballrooms, built for dinners and dancing, rarely get that care — which is why every keynote in one sounds like a lecture in a swimming pool.

items.alt: Leah and Maya, heads together by the airwall.

bubbles.text: Options. Fast.
One bus works, and it plays in both rooms. Plate B. The president goes there — or nowhere.

items.prompt: The keynote walks on in 20 seconds. One working bus, and it plays in both rooms. Who gets it?
items.happening: The system is COMBINED; only plate B's inputs reach any loudspeaker.
known: ◉ Room B's zone level is on its panel
items.risk: Four hundred people waiting for a keynote; three hundred sponsors who didn't ask for one.
timeout: The president walks on to silence and taps the microphone twice. Leah looks at you across the wall.
Waiting for the owner was right for the sensor; it was wrong for the walk-on. The bridge was yours.

hints.text: Which room's program is happening right now, and which one is only dessert?
A bridge is fine if the people it costs are told.

options.label: The keynote: patch into plate B too, mute the lunch mic, turn Room B's zone right down — and Leah tells the captain now
options.result: The president's first line lands in Room A. In Room B it's a murmur under the clink of dessert forks. Leah is already at the captain's elbow.
options.consequence: Sponsors hear a soft keynote for a few minutes. Their awards aren't until 2:15. It works; it isn't right; it's a bridge.

options.label: Re-patch everything to plate B and push it all up
options.result: The keynote booms through both rooms. The lunch emcee's toast disappears under it.
options.consequence: Two angry rooms instead of one.
options.fail: Turning everything up turned a routing problem into a room-relations problem.

options.label: Tell the hotel it's their system and wait
options.result: The president walks on to silence. “Can you hear me? …Can you hear me?”
options.fail: Blaming the hotel doesn't move a single sample. The bridge was yours to build.

options.label: Give the bus to the lunch; the president goes unamplified
options.result: The back half of Room A strains, then gives up.
options.consequence: The reason everyone is in Room A is the keynote.
options.fail: You protected the room with a dessert course and abandoned the room with a keynote.

items.alt: Room A: the president at the lectern, the audience listening. On the other side of the wall, Leah speaks quietly to the banquet captain.

bubbles.text: Good afternoon. Thank you all for coming back from lunch — some of you, I hear, are still at it.

items.caption: It works. It isn't right. It's a bridge, and everybody it costs has been told.

items.alt: Later, by the service door. Leah is quiet and angry; Maya takes it.

bubbles.text: “Easy one,” I said. Two rooms, one airwall. The captain just called us “the wire people.”
I labeled the brain of the wall at seven, and told nobody who had to move it.

items.caption: The low point isn't the silence. It's knowing the fix was a two-minute conversation at 7 a.m.

lines.text: The captain just called us “the wire people.”
Honestly? Today we are the wire people.

items.label: **Route it:** the path the keynote needs once the wall and the system agree.

items.alt: 1:44. The house tech has arrived at the wall pocket, sensor lead in hand, the plug an inch from the socket.

bubbles.text: Wedding ran short. I plug this in, the system divides instantly. No fade.
Wait. Don't. The keynote's on plate B right now.

items.title: The fix is a state change.
items.body: Right now the keynote rides plate B, because plate B is the only input COMBINED listens to. The instant the sensor is reconnected, the system goes DIVIDED — and in DIVIDED, plate B feeds only Room B. The president would vanish from Room A mid-sentence and play at full level into the sponsors' lunch. Fixing the state, done carelessly, would break both rooms at once.
items.label: Test: what has to be true before that plug goes in?

items.alt: System View in DIVIDED: the sensor reconnected reads CLOSED; plate A feeds only Room A's zones and plate B only Room B's. A note: keynote on A and B until the flip, mute B on the count.
items.caption: Put the program where the new state will look for it — before you change the state.

items.prompt: The house tech has the lead. When does it go in?
items.happening: The sensor lead is in the house tech's hand. The keynote is live on plate B.
known: ◉ Video roll at 1:52: two minutes with no live mic
◉ Your console can feed A and B at once
items.risk: Four hundred people mid-keynote; three hundred sponsors who've been patient.
timeout: The tech shrugs and plugs it in while you're thinking. The president vanishes from Room A mid-sentence.
An idle plan gets replaced by the nearest action. He was waiting for you to say when.

hints.text: When is the one moment in the keynote where nobody is speaking?
What would have to be on plate A already?

options.label: Now — the sooner the better
options.result: Click. DIVIDED. The president disappears from Room A mid-sentence and booms into the lunch.
options.consequence: Ten seconds of chaos in two rooms before you pull plate B.
options.fail: The right fix at the wrong moment is still a failure. A state change is a change.

options.label: At the 1:52 video roll, on a count: your feed already on plate A and B, your finger on plate B's mute
options.result: During the roll you add plate A. The tech counts; the plug goes in on “one”; you mute plate B on the click.
options.consequence: Room A never notices. Room B gets its room back.

options.label: After the keynote ends at 2:15
options.consequence: The sponsors' awards start at 2:15 — on a system that still thinks there's one room.
options.fail: You protected your client by postponing their problem into the other room.

options.label: Ask the tech to bypass the sensor and set DIVIDED from his laptop
options.result: He looks at you for a long second. “No.”
options.consequence: The sensor is how the system stays honest.
options.fail: Asking the owner to defeat his own interlock isn't a plan; it's a new failure mode.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #17 · AVERY'S LENS  Natural mapping  Controls should be laid out like the space they control.  A combine panel drawn as the actual ballroom — Room A left, Room B right, the airwall in between — prevents the wrong-room mistake.

items.alt: 1:52. The keynote's video rolls on the screen. Maya on the radio at the console end; the house tech at the pocket, counting on his fingers.

bubbles.text: Plate A's live, plate B's on my finger. Your count.
Three. Two. One. In.

lines.text: Plate A's live, plate B's on my finger. Your count.
(The house tech counts. Nobody breathes. It's the least dramatic thing that's ever felt this dramatic.)

items.alt: Room A's house panel, green now: DIVIDED, WALL: CLOSED. Maya exhales.
items.caption: The video never blinked. The system finally agrees with the wall.

items.alt: Room B. Maya stands at the back of the lunch listening; Leah gives a thumbs-up from the other door.

bubbles.text: Room B: only Room B. Room A: only the keynote.

The houseperson hands Maya the peeled-off label, a little crumpled from the vacuum wheel.

bubbles.text: Your label. Next time write what you actually want.
“Unplug me, then call Maya.” Printing it now.

items.caption: The label maker is Ray's. The lesson is too: a label is a message to the next person.

items.title: Printed on Ray's label maker
items.body: *UNPLUG ME — THEN CALL MAYA 555-0142.* The first label she's ever printed that asks for something instead of forbidding it. Ray would like it. She doesn't tell him. She should.

items.alt: The hotel lobby, afterward. Graham, a corporate client in a crisp suit, has come to meet Leah about next week.

bubbles.text: Next week. Hybrid product launch. Four thousand people online. Nobody in the room is allowed to notice.
Online's the easy part.

items.caption: Next: *Stems.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A divisible room is one system with several states, and every state has its own routing. When one room plays the other room, suspect the state before any cable: read the panel, listen in both rooms. The sensor, the interlock and any override belong to the venue. A state change is a change — put your program on the path the new state will use, count the change in with the owner, and verify in every room.

REFLECTION (optional)  · Maya did label the cable. She just wrote an instruction to people she never met, about a thing they had to do anyway. Who in your work touches your equipment when you are not there — and have you ever talked to them?  Boundary: this reflection proves nothing about the ballroom.
